title: Pre-Board Mock 1 (CBSE pattern)
subject: Science
instructions: This paper has 39 questions in 5 sections (A–E). All questions are compulsory. Internal choice is given in some questions.
Section A: Q1–Q20, 1 mark each (MCQs and Assertion–Reason). Section B: Q21–Q26, 2 marks each. Section C: Q27–Q33, 3 marks each.
Section D: Q34–Q36, 5 marks each. Section E: Q37–Q39, case-based, 4 marks each.
Write balanced equations, show formulae and units in numericals, and draw neat labelled diagrams wherever required.
This mock follows the reported 2026-27 pattern. Check the official CBSE sample paper for any changes.

sections.title: Section A
sections.note: Q1–Q16: choose the correct option. Q17–Q20: Assertion–Reason. For these, choose (a) both A and R true and R explains A; (b) both true but R does not explain A; (c) A true, R false; (d) A false, R true.

questions.q: Which of the following is a combination reaction?
questions.answer: (a) CaO + H_{2}O → Ca(OH)_{2}

questions.q: The pH of a solution is 13. The solution is:
questions.answer: (c) strongly basic

questions.q: Which of these metals does NOT give hydrogen gas with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.answer: (a) Copper (it is below hydrogen in the reactivity series)

questions.q: The name of the compound CH_{3}CHO is:
questions.answer: (c) ethanal (–CHO is the aldehyde group)

questions.q: Which of these has ten molecules of water of crystallisation?
questions.answer: (d) Washing soda, Na_{2}CO_{3}·10H_{2}O

questions.q: A few drops of phenolphthalein are added to sodium hydroxide solution. The colour of the solution becomes:
questions.answer: (b) pink

questions.q: Bile is poured into which part of the alimentary canal?
questions.answer: (b) Small intestine

questions.q: The correct path of urine in the human body is:
questions.answer: (c) Kidney → ureter → urinary bladder → urethra

questions.q: Which hormone prepares the body to deal with an emergency?
questions.answer: (a) Adrenaline

questions.q: Vegetative propagation by leaves is seen in:
questions.answer: (d) Bryophyllum (buds in the notches along the leaf margin)

questions.q: A cross between a heterozygous tall pea plant (Tt) and a short plant (tt) gives tall plants in the proportion:
questions.answer: (b) 50%. Offspring are Tt and tt in a 1 : 1 ratio.

questions.q: Which of the following is non-biodegradable?
questions.answer: (d) DDT

questions.q: A concave mirror forms a real image of the same size as the object. The object is placed:
questions.answer: (b) at C

questions.q: A wire of resistance 10 Ω is stretched uniformly to double its length. Its new resistance is:
questions.answer: (d) 40 Ω. The length doubles and the area halves, so R becomes 4 times.

questions.q: Which colour of white light is deviated the most by a glass prism?
questions.answer: (c) Violet

questions.q: The magnetic field lines inside a long, current-carrying solenoid are:
questions.answer: (a) parallel straight lines (a uniform field)

questions.q:
**Assertion (A):** Rancidity of food can be slowed down by keeping it in airtight containers.
**Reason (R):** Airtight containers reduce contact with oxygen, slowing the oxidation of fats and oils.

**Assertion (A):** Pepsin acts on proteins in the stomach.
**Reason (R):** The gastric glands secrete hydrochloric acid, which makes the medium in the stomach acidic, as needed for pepsin to act.

**Assertion (A):** A convex lens can form both real and virtual images.
**Reason (R):** A convex lens always forms the image on the side opposite to the object.
questions.answer: (c). A is true, but R is false: when the object is between F_{1} and O, the virtual image forms on the same side as the object.

questions.q:
**Assertion (A):** The concentration of pesticides is highest in organisms at the top of a food chain.
**Reason (R):** Pesticides are non-biodegradable and build up at each trophic level.
questions.answer: (a). This is biological magnification.

questions.q: What happens when silver chloride is kept in sunlight? Write the balanced equation and name the type of reaction.
questions.answer: White silver chloride turns grey. 2AgCl(s) → 2Ag(s) + Cl_{2}(g) in sunlight. This is a decomposition reaction caused by light (photolytic decomposition), used in black-and-white photography.

questions.q: In the electrolysis of water, name the gases collected at the cathode and the anode. Why is the volume of one gas double that of the other?
questions.answer: Hydrogen at the cathode and oxygen at the anode. Water (H_{2}O) has two hydrogen atoms for every oxygen atom: 2H_{2}O → 2H_{2} + O_{2}, so the volume of hydrogen is double.

questions.q: Give the function of: (a) villi in the small intestine, (b) salivary amylase.
questions.answer: (a) Villi increase the surface area for absorbing digested food, and are richly supplied with blood vessels. (b) Salivary amylase breaks down starch into simple sugar.

questions.q: Why do gametes have only half the number of chromosomes found in body cells?
questions.answer: When two gametes fuse, the zygote gets the full set of chromosomes, so the chromosome number of the species stays the same in every generation. Otherwise the number would double each generation.

or.answer: Every month the uterus prepares a thick, spongy lining to receive a fertilised egg. If the egg is not fertilised, the lining is not needed. It slowly breaks down and comes out through the vagina as blood and mucus. This happens roughly every month and lasts about 2–8 days.

questions.q: A 6 Ω and a 3 Ω resistor are connected in parallel, and this combination is connected in series with a 4 Ω resistor and a 6 V battery. Find the total resistance and the current drawn from the battery.
questions.answer: Parallel part: 1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2, so R = 2 Ω. Total = 2 + 4 = 6 Ω. I = V/R = 6/6 = 1 A.

or.q: The far point of a myopic person is 80 cm in front of the eye. What is the nature and power of the lens needed to correct the problem?
or.answer: A concave lens of focal length f = −80 cm = −0.8 m. P = 1/f = 1/(−0.8) = −1.25 D.

questions.q: Why are some substances biodegradable and others non-biodegradable? Give one example of each.
questions.answer: Biodegradable substances can be broken down by the enzymes of decomposers such as bacteria and fungi (e.g. fruit peels). Non-biodegradable substances cannot be broken down by these biological processes (e.g. plastic, DDT).

questions.q: Describe the electrolytic refining of copper.
questions.answer: Impure copper is made the anode and a thin strip of pure copper is made the cathode. The electrolyte is acidified copper sulphate solution. When current is passed, copper from the anode dissolves into the solution, and an equal amount of pure copper is deposited on the cathode. Soluble impurities go into the solution, and insoluble impurities settle at the bottom of the anode as anode mud.

questions.q: A compass needle is placed near a straight wire carrying current.

subparts.q: Why is the needle deflected?
subparts.answer: The current in the wire produces a magnetic field around it, which acts on the compass needle.

subparts.q: What happens to the deflection if the current is increased?
subparts.answer: The deflection increases (the field becomes stronger).

subparts.q: What happens to the deflection if the compass is moved farther from the wire?
subparts.answer: The deflection decreases (the field weakens with distance).

questions.q: An organic compound A with molecular formula C_{2}H_{4}O_{2} turns blue litmus red. It reacts with sodium carbonate to give a gas that turns lime water milky. Identify A and write the balanced equations for both reactions.
questions.answer: A is ethanoic acid (acetic acid), CH_{3}COOH. 2CH_{3}COOH + Na_{2}CO_{3} → 2CH_{3}COONa + H_{2}O + CO_{2}. The CO_{2} turns lime water milky: Ca(OH)_{2} + CO_{2} → CaCO_{3} + H_{2}O

questions.q: Describe the path of blood through the human heart, showing how double circulation works.
questions.answer: Deoxygenated blood from the body enters the right atrium through the vena cava, then goes to the right ventricle, which pumps it through the pulmonary artery to the lungs. Oxygenated blood returns through the pulmonary veins to the left atrium, then the left ventricle, which pumps it through the aorta to the body. Blood passes through the heart twice in each cycle, which is why it is called double circulation.

questions.q: You accidentally touch a hot plate and pull your hand away at once. Describe the reflex arc involved.
questions.answer: Heat receptors in the skin detect the stimulus. A sensory neuron carries the impulse to the spinal cord. A relay neuron in the spinal cord passes it to a motor neuron. The motor neuron carries the impulse to the arm muscles (effector), which contract and pull the hand away. The brain is informed later.

or.q: Give three differences between nervous control and hormonal control.
or.answer: Nervous control uses electrical impulses through neurons, while hormonal control uses chemical messengers through the blood. Nervous control is very fast, while hormonal control is slower. Nervous effects are short-lived, while hormonal effects last longer. Nervous impulses reach only the cells connected by nerves, while hormones reach all cells but act only on target cells.

questions.q: A 2 cm tall object is placed 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. Find the position, size and nature of the image.
questions.answer: u = −30 cm, f = +20 cm. 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/20 − 1/30 = 1/60, so v = +60 cm (on the other side of the lens). m = v/u = 60/(−30) = −2, so h′ = −4 cm. The image is real, inverted and magnified (4 cm tall).

or.q: A concave mirror produces a real image three times the size of an object placed 10 cm in front of it. Where is the image? Find the focal length of the mirror.
or.answer: Real image, so m = −3. m = −v/u gives v = 3u = 3 × (−10) = −30 cm, so the image is 30 cm in front of the mirror. 1/f = 1/v + 1/u = −1/30 − 1/10 = −4/30, so f = −7.5 cm.

questions.q: An electric heater is rated 1000 W, 220 V.

subparts.q: Find its resistance.
Find the current it draws.
How many units (kWh) does it use if run for 2 hours a day for 30 days?
subparts.answer: E = 1 kW × 2 h × 30 = 60 kWh (60 units)

questions.q: Answer the following:

subparts.q: Differentiate between saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons, with one example each. How can you tell them apart by burning?
subparts.answer: Saturated hydrocarbons have only single bonds between carbon atoms (e.g. ethane, C_{2}H_{6}). Unsaturated hydrocarbons have a double or triple bond (e.g. ethene, C_{2}H_{4}). On burning, saturated hydrocarbons give a clean blue flame, while unsaturated ones give a yellow, sooty flame.

subparts.q: Write the equation for the addition of hydrogen to ethene and state the condition needed.
subparts.answer: C_{2}H_{4} + H_{2} → C_{2}H_{6}, in the presence of a nickel (or palladium) catalyst.

or.q:
(a) Describe an activity to show that acids produce H^{+} ions only in water, using solutions of HCl, glucose and alcohol. [3]
(b) Why does distilled water not conduct electricity, while rain water does? [2]
or.answer: (a) Fix two nails on a cork in a beaker and connect them to a bulb and a battery through a switch. Pour in dilute HCl and switch on: the bulb glows. With glucose or alcohol solutions, the bulb does not glow, although they contain hydrogen. So acids produce H^{+} ions in solution, which carry the current. (b) Distilled water has no ions. Rain water contains dissolved acids and salts from the air, which give ions that conduct electricity.
marking: (b) no ions in distilled water 1, ions in rain water 1

questions.q: Answer the following:

subparts.q: Name the parts of the human male reproductive system and give the function of each.
subparts.answer: Testes: produce sperm and the hormone testosterone. Scrotum: holds the testes outside the body at a lower temperature, needed for sperm formation. Vas deferens: carries sperm. Urethra: common passage for sperm and urine. Seminal vesicles and prostate gland: add secretions so the sperm are in a fluid, which also provides nutrition.
marking: Any three parts with functions: 1 each

subparts.q: Give two changes seen in boys at puberty.
subparts.answer: (Any two) Hair grows on the face (moustache and beard). The voice begins to crack and becomes deeper. Hair grows in the armpits and genital area. Sudden increase in height and weight.

or.q:
(a) Explain how Amoeba obtains and digests its food. [3]
(b) Name the raw materials for photosynthesis, and say where a plant gets each of them. [2]
or.answer: (a) Amoeba pushes out finger-like extensions (pseudopodia) that surround the food particle and form a food vacuole. Inside the food vacuole, complex substances are broken down into simpler ones, which diffuse into the cytoplasm. Undigested material moves to the surface and is thrown out. (b) Carbon dioxide from the air, through the stomata. Water (and minerals) from the soil, through the roots. Sunlight is absorbed by chlorophyll.

questions.q: Answer the following:

subparts.q: Derive an expression for the equivalent resistance of three resistors R_{1}, R_{2} and R_{3} connected in series.
subparts.answer: In series the same current I flows through all the resistors, and the total voltage is the sum: V = V_{1} + V_{2} + V_{3}. By Ohm's law, IR_{s} = IR_{1} + IR_{2} + IR_{3}. Dividing by I: R_{s} = R_{1} + R_{2} + R_{3}.

subparts.q: A 4 Ω and a 12 Ω resistor are connected in parallel, and the combination is in series with a 3 Ω resistor across a 12 V battery. Find the total current.
subparts.answer: Parallel part: 1/R = 1/4 + 1/12 = 4/12, so R = 3 Ω. Total = 3 + 3 = 6 Ω. I = 12/6 = 2 A.

or.q:
(a) Derive an expression for the equivalent resistance of three resistors connected in parallel. [3]
(b) Why is tungsten used to make the filaments of electric bulbs? [2]
or.answer: (a) In parallel the voltage V across each resistor is the same, and the total current is the sum: I = I_{1} + I_{2} + I_{3}. So V/R_{p} = V/R_{1} + V/R_{2} + V/R_{3}, which gives 1/R_{p} = 1/R_{1} + 1/R_{2} + 1/R_{3}. (b) Tungsten has a very high melting point (3380 °C), so it does not melt when it is hot enough to glow and give light.
marking: (a) same V, currents add 1, substitution 1, result 1
(b) high melting point 1, glows without melting 1

sections.title: Section E
sections.note: Read each passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: Baking soda (sodium hydrogencarbonate) is commonly used in kitchens. When heated, it decomposes and releases carbon dioxide. If only baking soda is used in a cake, the cake rises but tastes bitter. So baking powder, a mixture of baking soda and a mild edible acid such as tartaric acid, is used instead.

subparts.q: Write the chemical formula of baking soda.
subparts.answer: NaHCO_{3}

subparts.q: Write the balanced equation for its decomposition on heating.
Why does a cake made with only baking soda taste bitter, and how does tartaric acid help?
subparts.answer: On heating, baking soda leaves behind sodium carbonate, which tastes bitter. Tartaric acid reacts with the baking soda to release CO_{2} without leaving sodium carbonate, so the cake rises and does not taste bitter.

questions.q: A student covered a healthy potted plant with a transparent polythene bag and tied it around the stem. After a few hours in sunlight, water droplets appeared on the inside of the bag.

subparts.q: Name the process that caused the droplets.
subparts.answer: Transpiration

subparts.q: Through which structures does most of this water leave the plant?
subparts.answer: The stomata in the leaves.

subparts.q: Give two ways in which this process helps the plant.
subparts.answer: It creates a suction (transpiration pull) that helps absorb water and minerals and move them up the xylem. It also cools the plant (temperature regulation).

questions.q: Spherical mirrors are used widely in daily life. Dentists and people shaving use one type of mirror. Vehicles use another type as rear-view mirrors because it gives a wider view of the traffic behind.

subparts.q: Which mirror is used as a shaving mirror, and why?
subparts.answer: Concave mirror. When the face is within its focus, it gives an enlarged, erect image.

subparts.q: Why is a convex mirror preferred as a rear-view mirror?
subparts.answer: It always gives an erect, diminished image and a much wider field of view.

subparts.q: A convex rear-view mirror has a radius of curvature of 3.00 m. A bus is 5.00 m behind it. Find the position of the image.
subparts.answer: f = R/2 = +1.50 m, u = −5.00 m. 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 1/1.5 + 1/5 = 13/15, so v ≈ +1.15 m. The image is 1.15 m behind the mirror (virtual, erect).

closing: All the best for your boards!
